passage_of_record.quote: Sign 532 and sign 297 are positioned in such a way as to resemble the position of the graphic element and several of their features are repeated in the image field. It is proposed here that sign 532 is a logograph for the anthropomorphic figure and that sign 297 represents the horned tiger, or perhaps just 'tiger' generically.

descriptor.text: Sign 297 is a bundle of four long parallel strokes bent once: the upper portions slant steeply down to the left; below the bend the strokes run near-vertical and splay slightly apart at the base. It stands in the plates' bent-ray run (signs 289-308), whose members differ in stroke count, bend position, and basal splay.
descriptor.derivation: Glyph inspection of the thesis plate (plate_reference below), in the Phase-123 manner. In Spec 064 the descriptor is derived twice independently under the frozen protocol's step D and checked against this record; this record is checked, not inherited.
descriptor.recorded_limitation: The descriptor fixes the family and the sign's place in the run; unique discrimination against the nearest neighbours (296, 299, 302-306) is fine-grained and is a separately checked step of the successor protocol (step C), with IDENTIFICATION FAILED pre-registered if the two independent derivations disagree.

continuity_status.basis: Anchored at family level only. No record the program holds anchors the number 297 individually from the 2015 side: there is no formation text for 297 (the held text's only '297' is the passage itself), no registry row, and no witness row.
